summary:
# NOTES: *Pride and His Prisoners* (A. L. O. E.; one book)

**Front matter:** Thomas Nelson and Sons (London, Edinburgh, New York). Frontispiece "A Terrible Danger" (p.230). Other plates: "Her greeting to Dr. and Miss Bardon was most gracious and cordial" (p.57); "Tearing the Manuscript" (p.107); "An Unwelcome Surprise" (p.168). 30 chapters.

## Frame (Ch I–III)
- Spring Sabbath, Somersetshire. **Nettleby Tower**: Norman robber-hold on hill; moat dry, portcullis rusted; Commonwealth siege bullet marks. Ruined by lawsuit and family dissension. Owner **Mr. Auger** (Thomas Auger) never lived there.
- Rightful heir **Timon Bardon** disinherited by proud, intemperate father (last Mr. Bardon) for marrying a farmer's daughter, 30+ years earlier. Old woman guide says Dr. Bardon lives in "small grey speck" below.
- Tower "haunted" by **Pride** (tall, dark, deep voice, bat-like wing) and **Intemperance** (wild red-meteor light, mirthful jarring laugh). Narrator personifies them.
- Pride's claims: caused Hugh Bardon's disinheriting; keeps "fermentation" stages (vinous = high spirit; acid = brooding sourness; third = hated, self-worshipping rebel). Pride enters church unseen, tarnishes offerings, writes false epitaphs. Only foe he fears: Gospel spirit ("David and Goliath"). Pride's arts: "pardonable weakness", "natural instinct", "generous virtue".
- Intemperance: "snowdrop" image; Pride: "snowdrop has its roots in the earth".
- Footnote joke: lady to pastor "What a beautiful sermon"; pastor: "The devil told me the very same thing."
- Pride targets **Ida Aumerle**, pastor's daughter; "dark soft eye", "Ithuriel's spear".
- Ch II: Ida lost mother at 12; younger sister **Mabel** (clever, impulsive). Ida vain of mirror/dress, then conversion ("birth of a soul") one evening while reading Bible. At ~18, stayed at **Aspendale** with uncle **Augustine Aumerle**; met **Reginald, Earl of Dashleigh** (Augustine's Cambridge friend; seat visible in blue distance). Ida refused Dashleigh; he then proposed to Ida's cousin **Annabella**. Ida's father **Lawrence Aumerle** (vicar of Ayrley) remarried **Miss Lambert** (now **Mrs. Aumerle / Barbara**), practical, sensible, stout, high-coloured. Ida dethroned; Pride calls her resentment "sensitiveness".
- Ch III: Anthem dispute: Ida taught trio to three girls; Mrs. Aumerle condemned it; Ida gave up choir music "at my suggestion" (Pride). Lawrence once prosperous, self-satisfied; his first wife died of sickness, he was humbled. Augustine: handsome, brilliant, Cambridge honours, German philosophy, drifts to scepticism; Pride "leads him" to be sceptic. Authorial preface: first three chapters as dialogue preface.

## BOOK (Ch IV–XXX), chronological

**Ch IV – Mill Cottage.** Two-storey stone cottage, iron knocker, polyanthus garden. Sitting-room: deal table, tidies, watercolours, guitar-box with pink ribbon, miniatures, china figures (one armless, one headless), gaily bound books. **Cecilia Bardon** (30–40; sallow, light hair, grey eyes; dress-proud; chose fawn kid boots over curtain and school subscription). **Dr. Timon Bardon** (black brows, white hair to shoulders, mouth corners turned down, "leonine"). Card-rack holds **Annabella's wedding cards** (married 1 yr 10 months). Doctor: "she'd have managed to come four miles." Doctor: "It's the fool that gets on in the world." Ida and Mabel bring a crimson curtain for Bardon's cold room. Bardon grudging. Annabella's invitation to Dashleigh Hall via girls. Doctor insists "Mill Cottage" not "Milton"; gives hyacinths to girls.

**Ch V – Both Sides.** Mabel: doctor's "mental glass" (Pride's patent: magnifies own, diminishes others'). Mabel: world = "porcelain" (Sèvres) vs "crockery"; Mrs. Aumerle "crockery". Ida's farm-boy class plan (Saturdays) conflicts with Mrs. Aumerle's mothers' class. Mrs. Aumerle snipping clothes: "not proper" to cross fields after sunset. Mrs. Aumerle: "Your father's daughter teaching... hulking farm lads." Compromise: Mrs. Aumerle takes lads; Ida gets mothers' meeting; Ida reluctantly agrees. Ida quotes James 4 ("God resisteth the proud").

**Ch VI – The Visit to the Hall.** Doctor yields on third day. Transport: donkey-chaise from farmer neighbour (not clarence from Pelton, 6 miles). Cecilia in flounced silk, dust-anxious. Lodge-keeper **Mills**. Hall = "mere gingerbread" (doctor). Annabella: below-middle height, "Titania", vivacious dark eyes, irregular profile, ink on finger, writing romance. Doctor won by request for **Venice Sumach** slip. Cecilia: "not a particle of pride."

**Ch VII – A Misadventure.** Annabella: orphan, grandmother's pet; pen-name **"Egeria"**; ambition for press. Dashleigh proposed partly from pique. Marriage soured; Pride whispers to each spouse (she: "vulgar"; he: "weak, obstinate", "accident of birth"). Dashleigh: vertigo, fastidious pride, "twelfth Earl of Dashleigh". Duke of **Montleroy** invited to luncheon. Earl angry at "low people" (Bardons in chaise); butler: "covers for four". Earl demands wife come; she delays. Doctor/Cecilia leave; overheard by library door: "Can't you manage some way of getting rid of these miserable Bardons?" Doctor's blast ("Who is miserable... slave of pride... I retort"). Annabella weeps.

**Ch VIII – A Brother's Effort.** Vicarage evening. Lawrence and Augustine in study. Augustine's Bible remark at dinner. Augustine: "I have discovered... paths besides the dry beaten one." Argument on reason vs. faith; electricity, memory, "infancy of our existence" (child-king simile). Lawrence reads **Psalm 131**. Augustine: origin of sin; Lawrence: "trace effects of sin in my own heart"; "Spiritual pride... ignorance". Augustine: "Lawrence, we have had enough." Augustine plays Tennyson critique to nieces; Lawrence prays.

**Ch IX – Disappointment.** Annabella revising proofs of romance (violet and gold). Earl disapproves authorship; Swiss mountain incident recalled (earl stuck, she gave her hand/boa). Annabella: proceeds to donate to church gallery. Earl: "Grub Street... House of Lords." Earl permits only private circulation; she refuses. "Tyrant!" (Pride whispers). Annabella writes satirical "The Precipice and the Peer" (Earl of ——; Albert Smith reference; boa rescue) in revenge; leaves in desk drawer.

**Ch X – On the Watch.** April afternoon in arbour. Augustine: Ida "too good". Mabel's "ladder of good works" broken; Ida: "bright golden cord", faith. Prayer insincerity; "dearest idol" hymn. Mabel's head on Ida's bosom; Pride baffled.

**Ch XI – The Quarrel.** Boudoir: Earl tells of Augustine's balloon, **Verdon** (æronaut, schoolfellow); trial ascent of the ***Eaglet*** from Aspendale grounds. Annabella teases earl about boa; earl insists he'll go. Earl finds manuscript "The Precipice and the Peer" in drawer; tears and tramples it. "Leave the room, insolent girl!" Duke of Montleroy witnesses. Annabella's maid **Bates**; coachman **Mullins**; she orders carriage, will sleep at vicarage. Servants gossip (butler: "odd couple" with donkey-chaise). Annabella: Mr. Aumerle's late wife was her aunt (mother's sister).

**Ch XII – The Unexpected Guest.** Evening at vicarage: Bardon brings crystallised pebble; plays chess with Mrs. Aumerle. Cecilia sings "Bel raggio lusinghier" badly. Mabel asks to fly in balloon; Mrs. Aumerle: "That's pride." Augustine invites Bardon/Cecilia to ascent; earl also invited. Bardon: "I would sit down with... but not... Reginald Earl of Dashleigh." Dashleigh's red liveries seen; Mabel slips the name. Annabella arrives haggard; to study with Lawrence. Ida moves to share with Mabel. Bardon: "I'd rather have him for my enemy."

**Ch XIII – The Friend's Mission.** Mabel and Mrs. Aumerle quarrel ("a woman's spirit ought to be one of submission"; "child of fifteen... silence"). Mrs. Aumerle lacks "feelers". Ida's influence blamed. Augustine's mission to earl: earl will pardon only if Annabella asks forgiveness and returns that day. Augustine declines to go to Annabella, leaves for Aspendale. Annabella: "Forgiveness to the injured doth belong..." refuses to beg pardon. Doctor summoned.

**Ch XIV – A Fatal Step.** Doctor and Annabella alone. Gossip version: Papists, nun, mass, Virgin prayer (false). Doctor: "Write out that paper again... It would be revenge!" Doctor gave her "something to compose." Ida knocks: "I wish to be alone." Two envelopes sealed: "The Precipice and the Peer" to magazine editor; letter to London publisher authorising printing under "Countess of Dashleigh". Ring memory. Mabel offers to recall Bates; Annabella says "No" (fear Ida's letter seen). Ida hesitates, doesn't enter. Bates posts letters.

**Ch XV – The Deserted Home.** Earl lonely; regrets; Pride insists wife must apologise first. Breakfast: magazine ad "Now in the press: THE FAIRY LAKE. By the COUNTESS OF DASHLEIGH." Reads satire; groans. Letter from Lawrence pleading for Annabella. Earl writes note to Augustine ("DEAR AUMERLE... a place in the car... 12th" signed "DASHLEIGH").

**Ch XVI – Pleading.** Annabella confesses: wrote to editor to stop, too late. Ida: "bridge of hope... trembling." Annabella: "I cannot play the part of a penitent child." Ida: pride quotations; Annabella: "saintly cousin... not perfect in submission." Mrs. Aumerle enters: rebukes Annabella; Annabella: "I will not remain... to be insulted." Orders Bates to pack, go to Mill Cottage. Mabel clings. Annabella leaves on foot. Ida: "it was your coming that changed all!" Ida's regret for omission.

**Ch XVII – Conscience Asleep.** Bardon's religion pervasive pride/hate; "good hater"; "Forgive us... as we forgive" hypocrisy. Bardon eager for magazine. Walks six miles to Pelton (library). Librarian: magazine sold out; article "hit on a leading man"; pen guessed. Bardon: "She's done it!"

**Ch XVIII – The Magazine.** Baker's boy and page reading it; page: "It's my master's." Mrs. Clayton (blind major's widow, green blinds) has the magazine; her cochlico/rheumatism complaints. Bardon reads, laughs. Death notice in *Times*: "Mr. Auger, of —— Street and Nettleby Tower" dead; Bardon gloats. Annabella arrives at Mill Cottage; Bardon welcomes her. Cecilia sacrifices white muslin robe, best bow, garden flowers. Bates scorns cottage ("no footman kept"). Annabella accepts "as if from childhood." Cecilia: "not a particle of pride!"

**Ch XIX – Expectation.** Rumour: earl to ascend in *Eaglet* (12 May). Annabella gloomy, won't eat. Doctor resolves to attend. Mabel wins father's grudging permission ("ask your mother's opinion"); Mrs. Aumerle: "No." Ida has qualms. Vicar to wife: "I daresay, my love, you were right."

**Ch XX – A Sunny Morn.** 12 May dawn. Mabel leaves early; Augustine arrives in gig with horse **Black Prince**. Ida declines (Augustine asks; Mabel says no). Passing Mill Cottage. Augustine: earl's "want of good taste". Augustine: earl "plunged into rapid stream... fought a bully". Mabel: "Pride, I suppose." Aspendale Lodge (slope, daisy meadow). Verdon: small, sharp features, keen grey eyes. Mabel does honours. Doctor: "Has the earl come?"; "wind... toward Mill Cottage." Crowd of villagers. Earl's chariot with red liveries arrives; earl pale, silent.

**Ch XXI – The Ascent.** Guillotine simile. Earl not a coward but dizzy at heights. Augustine: "not fit to ascend." Earl gulps wine. Earl sees Bardon's sarcastic smile; enters car. Earl grabs to get out; struggles; "Let go!" shouted; men release ropes; balloon shoots up. Verdon: "Merciful Heaven! they are lost!" Verdon was not in car (signal too soon). Bardon rides off on borrowed horse ("How shall I tell this to Annabella?").

**Ch XXII – In the Clouds.** Augustine pulls valve rope; it snaps; no means to release gas. Cloud/mist; paper falls like lead. Augustine's prayer. Sea of cloud; Dashleigh Hall a toy. Earl prostrate. Cork explodes (wine); earl frantic, tries to leap; whirlwind spins balloon; earl faints.

**Ch XXIII – Regrets.** Ida regrets not stopping Mabel; asks vicar to visit Annabella. Bardon rides up: "Lost! lost!"; reports Augustine, Mabel, Dashleigh aboard. Annabella's cry. Vicar prays. Cecilia sees balloon. Annabella upbraids Bardon: "never, never enter my presence."

**Ch XXIV – Soaring above Pride.** Sunset; earl calm, sees "letters on the wall"; Assyrian/Nebuchadnezzar and Saul comparisons. Knife attempts fail. Mabel writes farewell letter (to father, Ida, step-mother; asks Mrs. Aumerle's pardon); drops it. Earl drops pocket-book (gold shield, coronet; Annabella's first gift); pencils two words in it. Earl's text: "The loftiness of man shall be bowed down..." (Isa. 2:17). Night; Augustine can't pray; earl leads Litany ("Lord, deliver us"). Augustine's inner confession: intellect as idol, pride as priest.

**Ch XXV – A Broken Chain.** Annabella's grief (tears hair, strikes bosom). Ida's prayer in Mabel's room (Ida's sketch, lilac, Bible birthday gift). Mrs. Aumerle: "I believe there were faults on both sides." Ida confesses ("I felt it difficult to urge... a duty I had neglected myself"). Mrs. Aumerle embraces Ida. Pride flees: "chain... broken."

**Ch XXVI – The Awful Crisis.** Augustine's night reflection (Pride vs faith; "without the one sacrifice"). Dawn; balloon less full. Augustine sees sea. Ballast bag thrown; instrument box; basket; grappling irons. Balloon sinks; Augustine cuts ropes with Dashleigh's knife. Car torn free, floats, baled with Mabel's straw hat and Dashleigh's beaver. Balloon rises free. Mabel: "Pride..." image. Prolonged exposure; Dashleigh prays for a young widow. Sail sighted; Augustine waves kerchief; ship answers.

**Ch XXVII – Tidings.** Morning at vicarage; postman brings *The Fairy Lake* for countess. Annabella writes to publisher cancelling whole edition (her losses). Callers refused. Telegram from Cliff Cottage, B——, Devon: "Safe, thank God! I shall send M—— home to-morrow. I remain here with the earl, who is attacked by brain fever. I have telegraphed to Exeter for Dr. G—— and a nurse.—A. A." Annabella insists on going; Lawrence escorts her; Mrs. Aumerle keeps Ida home (later Ida goes). Mrs. Aumerle's sarcastic soliloquy on Augustine and the "poor earl." Mabel's letter found by farmer, posted; Mrs. Aumerle softened: "let bygones be bygones."

**Ch XXVIII – The Wheel Turns.** Cecilia & doctor unhappy; chicken, tartlets, "bills". Doctor fears earl fell out of balloon. Letter (black seal): executors of Thomas Auger bequeath **Nettleby Tower** to Timon Bardon plus reimbursement of lawsuit cost. Doctor's remorse. Train; night arrival at Devon station; chaise took doctor and nurse to Cliff Cottage; fishing-smack rescued three. Party walks up gorge; "valley of the shadow of death." Driver: "A gentleman is ill; doctor is staying." Shingle fisherman's cottage by sea; Mabel reunited with father.

**Ch XXIX – Two Words.** Dr. G—— (tall, bald, black coat) forbids Annabella access ("high fever"). Gentlemen sleep on kitchen floor (fishy); Annabella, Ida, Mabel in tiny room. Augustine nurses earl. Augustine & Lawrence on beach: Augustine: "Tribulation worketh patience..."; Lawrence: "hope... is it your own?" Augustine silently assents. Mabel and Lawrence leave. Earl's illness; Annabella humbled. Pocket-book (mud-stained) returned via Dashleigh Hall; Ida finds two pencilled words: **"forgiveness" and "peace"**. Earl forgives in fisherman's hut; Annabella's penitent reunion.

**Ch XXX – The Spirit Laid.** July. Earl convalescent at Dashleigh Hall boudoir; reading *The Fairy Lake*. Annabella now deferential. Earl proposes returning Bardon's visit. Tower party (Aumerles, Ida, Mabel, Augustine, Bardon, Cecilia). Cecilia displays Mill Cottage's remaining rubbish; Mabel points at Mill Cottage; Dashleigh's carriage approaches. Augustine's "haunted new houses" reply. Dashleigh extends hand; Bardon grasps it; "from that hour the evil spirit of enmity... was laid for ever."
- Authorial coda: Pride is a life-long campaign; forms (purse, person, family, national, spiritual pride). Long poem on Pride ("Proud,—and of what?..."). Final admonition: "clip the soaring wing of the *Eaglet*—cut the cords of your balloon!"
